claims.claim: Every named primitive is either mapped to an exact spec-list failure class or dropped; dropped_unmapped_count=1.
claims.strongest_caveat: The spec list is the four classes named in the unit question, not the unread 47-line _USER-PROMPTS.md table. FC-11317 has no mapped primitive from this list.

claims.claim: Idempotency keys map to duplicate-dispatch via MillWheel unique record IDs (§6.1.1) with a paired latency baseline in §8.1.
claims.strongest_caveat: §8.1 measures latency cost, not duplicate-dispatch count on this estate. Structural mapping is confirmed; incidence transfer is not.

claims.claim: Fencing tokens have a published zombie-write rejection rate versus an unfenced baseline and may be promoted.
claims.strongest_caveat: §6.2 describes sequencer tokens; it does not report a count. Mapped to FC-11315, graded E3, not promoted.

claims.claim: Lease expiry maps to FC-11315 (stale monitor / dispatcher death), not to FC-11317, because TST-0090 binds reclaim-after-expiry to the dead dispatcher rather than to a live hung sibling.
claims.strongest_caveat: Gray Figure 1 numbers are cache-consistency traffic on the V system. Catalog 51154/61321 assign 11317 to per-unit pipelines.

claims.claim: Exactly-once illusions are a distinct primitive that maps onto duplicate-dispatch independently of idempotency keys.
claims.strongest_caveat: MillWheel: the guarantee does not extend to external systems. Dropped as unmapped-as-distinct-primitive.

claims.claim: BBR's 2–25× vs CUBIC on Google B4 proves this estate's 429 storms are closed by deploying BBR.
claims.strongest_caveat: Wrong layer (TCP goodput vs HTTP 429). Backpressure still maps structurally to FC-11318; the BBR number does not transfer.

claims.claim: Third-hand IRJMETS citation of Stripe reducing duplicates from 0.5% to 0.001% may promote idempotency keys.
claims.strongest_caveat: No primary Stripe measurement captured. Headline without a re-checkable baseline is E3 and cannot promote.

control.name: unmapped-primitive-must-drop
control.note: Two-phase commit is a real DS primitive. It does not address duplicate-dispatch, stale-monitor, hung-batch, or 429-storm on the spec list, so it is dropped. A mapper that force-fits it onto duplicate-dispatch is rejected.

dropped.reason: MillWheel §6.1.1: the exactly-once guarantee does not extend to external systems. This program's artifacts are external JSON files. Framework exactly-once is at-least-once plus idempotent sinks — the idempotency-key primitive already mapped. Treating the illusion as a fifth distinct mapping would be elegance.

e3_records.why_e3: Headline mechanism without a reported zombie-write rejection count versus an unfenced baseline. E3: mapped, not promoted.
Dropped as unmapped-as-distinct-primitive. §8.1 latency numbers belong to the idempotency-key envelope already promoted, not to a second class mapping.

mechanisms.baseline: same pipeline with exactly-once and strong productions OFF: median 3.6 ms, p95 30 ms
mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: MillWheel §6.1.1 unique record IDs journaled in the same atomic write as state; retried deliveries with the same ID are discarded. That is an idempotency key on dispatch. This program's duplicate-dispatch class is the same shape: a second dispatch of one unit must not produce a second receipt.
mechanisms.effect_size: exactly-once + strong productions ON: median 33.7 ms, p95 93.8 ms (200 CPUs)

source_lineage.title: MillWheel: Fault-Tolerant Stream Processing at Internet Scale

mechanisms.strongest_caveat: The paired number is latency cost of the dedup envelope, not a counted reduction in duplicate dispatches. §6.1.1 is structural; it reports no duplicate-discard count. Transfer to this estate is unmeasured.

mechanisms.baseline: zero-term lease (callback on every access); infinite-term as the other bound. Trace: consistency is 30% of server traffic at zero term
mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: Gray & Cheriton: an unreachable leaseholder blocks writers only until the term expires. GFS §3.1: after a 60 s chunk lease expires the master may grant a new primary. TST-0090: when the dispatcher holding a unit lease dies, reclaim is allowed only after expiry. That is monitor/dispatcher death (11315), not the 11317 live-hang barrier.
mechanisms.effect_size: S=1, 10 s term: consistency traffic is 10% of zero-term; total server traffic 27% below zero-term and 4.5% above infinite-term
mechanisms.failure_class_exact_name: stall detection from mtimes alone is impossible / orchestrator death

source_lineage.title: Leases: An Efficient Fault-Tolerant Mechanism for Distributed File Cache Consistency

mechanisms.strongest_caveat: Gray numbers are V-system file-cache consistency traffic, not orchestrator reclaim latency. This program's 11317 (hung unit blocks a batch) is assigned by the catalog to per-unit pipelines, not to leases; lease is bound here to 11315 per TST-0090.

mechanisms.baseline: CUBIC on the same B4 prober (8 MB every minute) and on the 100 Mbps / 100 ms lab link; CUBIC drops 10× at 0.1% loss and stalls above 1%
mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: BBR is sender-side admission that slows when the path is saturated instead of bursting into loss. FC-11318 is a 429 arrival-rate storm: naive fan-out bursts into provider quota. The shared primitive is backpressure / admission control with a measured competing baseline (CUBIC).
mechanisms.effect_size: B4 production: BBR throughput 2–25× CUBIC; one US-Europe path BBR 2 Gbps vs CUBIC 15 Mbps (133×). Figure 8: BBR holds the (1-lossRate) limit up to 5% random loss
mechanisms.strongest_caveat: BBR measures TCP goodput, not HTTP 429 counts on this estate. The mapping is structural (admission vs burst), not a measured 429-storm close.
